skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: The opening warning at T2 covers the Committee and company as the client, that counsel does not represent the witness personally and cannot advise him, and that the company may disclose without his consent. It comes at the very start of the interview.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 states that the privilege belongs to the company, which decides whether to waive it and may disclose what is learned without the witness's consent. T4 then checks the witness's understanding of who controls the privilege.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 explains how the interview will proceed, asks for complete answers, sets ground rules on speculation and estimates, and asks the witness to distinguish recollection from reconstruction.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T4 asks the witness to restate in his own words who is represented and who controls privilege, and T6 confirms he may consult his own lawyer. The witness's reply at T3 about possibly wanting his own counsel is acknowledged.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T356 gives a confidentiality reminder, a document-retention instruction, a no-discussion-with-witnesses instruction and 'We may follow up', and asks 'Anything to add or correct?'. It does not expressly ask whether there is 'nothing else' beyond the wrap-up question.

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
The company decides whether to waive it, and it may disclose what we learn, including to the government, without your consent and without telling you.
Before we go on, could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?
A few ground rules: if you're speculating, assuming, or estimating, please tell me.
Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses. We may follow up. Anything to add or correct?

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: The interviewer repeatedly asks the witness to walk through events openly, for example 'Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999' (T16), and does the same for the Rhythms unwind, Chewco, the LJM2 controls and the Chewco tax payment.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The interview moves from role and reporting lines (T8-T14) to open topics and then to specific points such as the November 5, 1997 call (T58) and the Southampton purchase. A few specific questions are asked before the general picture is complete.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are short and clear, such as 'Who negotiated the unwind for Enron?' (T34). Some are wordy or double-barrelled, such as T22 and T332's summary, and 'Help me understand how those fit together' is used repeatedly rather than a precise question.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The interviewer stays calm, neutral and polite throughout, including when the witness deflects (T262-T265) and when confronted with the Chewco note (T306). The interviewer keeps control of the sequence.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer changes approach as answers develop. They switch from open narrative to documents when answers are vague (T70, T128, T194, T300), follow the witness's estimates with 'What's your best estimate?' (T118), and turn to the Southampton and Chewco contradictions once they emerge.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
How did those reviews work in practice? Take a specific deal.
Take Raptor I. What did Mr. Causey and Mr. Buy actually review before they signed its approval sheet?
What's your best estimate?
How do you know that: did you see it yourself, or did someone tell you?
Our information is that Talon hadn't yet done any derivatives with Enron. Help me understand how those fit together.

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: The interviewer follows up on evasive or inconsistent answers, including the witness's 'I don't believe it came up' on Board disclosure (T163-T169), the Raptor 'tremendous utilization' statement (T252), the 'stayed out of it' claim against the $10.5 million note (T306-T308), and the Southampton returns (T141-T145).

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The interviewer establishes who negotiated the unwind and Chewco, the dates of the Southampton and Raptor approvals, and the amounts. Some details were left unpinned, such as the approval-sheet signature gaps and the timing of Board knowledge.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: The interviewer uses documents to refresh memory (minutes at T70, the Southampton agreement at T128, the LJM2 report at T194 and the note at T300) and asks about notes at T62. The witness's 'I don't remember the individual names' (T41) is answered by redirecting to Causey rather than by other memory aids.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: The interviewer separates first-hand from second-hand knowledge: 'How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?' (T56) leads to 'I don't know that personally' (T57), and T346 asks 'did you see it yourself, or did someone tell you?'. The Chewco and approval-sheet knowledge is also separated.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: The interviewer asks who else should be spoken with (T336) and who would know about the Chewco figure (T338). Follow-up at T340-T343 identifies Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, McMahon, Skilling and Lay with their roles.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: The interviewer asks about minutes (T62), the deal files and approval sheets (T349), the Foundation's account statements (T350), and personal notes and emails (T352-T355), and asks that they be kept (T356).

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: The interviewer asks how certain the witness is on key points: 'How certain are you of that figure?' (T144), 'How sure are you of that figure?' (T216), 'How confident are you in that number?' (T222), and 'How sure are you about the timing?' (T318).

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Material answers are followed up consistently, such as the Foundation's $4.5 million (T142-T150), the Southampton investment's Board disclosure (T162-T169), the Raptor return comparison (T200-T210), and the summary of the tax-payment call (T332). One possible follow-up was not pursued, the witness's claim that Skilling's line on the Raptor I approval sheet was blank (T103).

moments.text: How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
I don't know that personally. That was my understanding.
How certain are you of that figure?
Follow-up on the Foundation's May 1, 2000 receipt of about $4.5 million on its $25,000 investment, testing the witness's figure after his vague 'a few million' answer.
Asks what Causey and Buy could say about how approvals worked in practice, and what Lay and Skilling could say about the LJM approvals (T342), identifying further witnesses.
Asks what documents should be reviewed and the witness identifies the approval sheets, Board and Finance Committee materials, and partnership agreements.
Asks about personal files, notes or emails and the witness discloses personal notes and emails about LJM and Southampton, which are then located (T355).
How sure are you about the timing?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: Documents are introduced with context and authenticated: the minutes are shown and provenance asked (T70-T72), the Southampton agreement's date, drafter and signature are confirmed (T128-T135), and the LJM2 report is confirmed as a complete copy (T194-T199).

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: Documents are shown only after the witness has given an account. Before the LJM2 report, the interviewer asks what returns the Board expected (T110-T114) and what LJM2 actually earned (T112), and before the April 2001 communication asks what was said to investors (T254-T255).

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: Document descriptions match the case record: the Southampton agreement is dated March 20, 2000 (T128), the Foundation's $4.5 million distribution is dated May 1, 2000 (T142), the April 2001 quote is accurate (T260), and the Raptor IRRs of 193, 278 and 2,500 percent are accurately presented (T200).

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: The interviewer generally avoids drawing conclusions from documents and asks the witness to reconcile differences, for example 'Help me understand how those fit together' (T306) and 'Help me understand the difference' (T242). The disclaimer 'I'm not suggesting you wrote it' (T300) is accurate.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: The witness gets room to explain: 'Help me understand how those fit together' (T150) is followed by the full answer at T151, the note contradiction at T306 is followed by the witness's explanation at T307, and the Raptor 'tremendous utilization' point at T252 is followed by an explanation at T253.

moments.text: I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
I'm now going to show you a document: a partnership agreement for Southampton Place, dated March 20, 2000. Do you recognize it?
Before showing the LJM2 October 2000 report, the interviewer asks what figures LJM2 reported to its investors, and the witness says 'well above 30 percent on the early ones' (T193).
I'm not suggesting you wrote it. Do you recognize it?
Earlier you told me you stayed out of the Chewco buyout. This note, addressed to 'Andy,' refers to $10.5 million for the buyout. Help me understand how those fit together.
It says their return 'was not at risk' because LJM2 'had already received its return of and on capital.' Is that what you told them?

missed_opportunities: T103: The witness said Skilling's line on the Raptor I approval sheet was left blank, which conflicts with his earlier claim that Skilling approved the Chewco and LJM matters (T55) and his later statement that he did not recall telling anyone Skilling approved the $10 million figure (T286-T287). The interviewer did not pursue this inconsistency.

T343: The witness said 'Ken relied on Jeff and me for the details.' The interviewer did not ask what Lay was told about LJM2 returns, the Southampton investment or the Chewco figure, even though this bore directly on whether the Board was accurately informed.
tips: When a witness says an approval was signed after closing or that a signature line was blank, what exact sheet, date and signer would you ask them to confirm before moving on?
When the witness says 'I believe' or 'I don't recall', what would you ask next to separate what they personally saw from what they were told, and what document would they need to check first?
